nominees.name: Eric A. Swanson
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (formerly MIT Lincoln Laboratory), USA

motivation: In 1991 Fujimoto, Huang and Swanson showed that low-coherence interferometry with broadband light can map the internal structure of living tissue in three dimensions at micrometre resolution, without contact or ionizing radiation. OCT turned the physics of ultrashort pulses and optical coherence into a new way to see inside the body. Their later advances, Fourier-domain detection, swept sources and fibre-optic implementations, raised imaging speed by orders of magnitude. OCT is now the standard of care in ophthalmology, with tens of millions of scans every year, and is spreading into cardiology, dermatology and endoscopy. It shows clearly how curiosity-driven research in laser physics and interferometry can grow into a technology that protects the sight and health of people around the world. It is an optical invention of the greatest benefit to humankind.
